texts.preamble: Anamika Jha vs Mayank Mrinal on 7 February, 2025 Kabc080042162021 Presented on : 19-08-2021 Registered on : 19-08-2021 Decided on : 07-02-2025 Duration : 3 years, 5 months, 19 days In The Court Of The Judicial Magistrate First Class (Traffic Court-Vi), Bengaluru City. Dated This 7Th Day Of February 2025.
texts.facts: The present petition is filed by the petitioner under Sec.12 of Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005. 2. The brief facts of the petitioner's case are as under; The Petitioner and the respondent No.1 are husband and wife and their marriage was solemnized on 29.04.2016 at Crl.Misc.88/2021 VSK Garden, Greater Noida, U.P. and from the wedlock they have one child. Further she submitted that, at the time of marriage respondents family had given some gold ornaments to the petitioner and her parents also given some gold ornaments to the respondent no.1 and to her. After marriage she started to live with respondents at matrimonial house and on 09.05.2016 respondent No.2 demanded all jewels given to her and she handed over the all the jewellery and money to respondent No.2. Further she submitted that, respondent No.2 took away all the gifts and money which the petitioner had received on her wedding. Further she submitted that, on 11.05.2016 petitioner and respondent No.1 went to her parents house at Lucknow for the first time after their marriage and at that time respondent No.1 and respondent No.2 were taunting the petitioner constantly on minor things. Petitioner went back to Delhi to her matrimonial home on 19.05.2016 along with her father. At that time respondent No.1 had already left for his office and respondent No.2 demanded a bed from her father and respondent No.2 purchased a bed for Rs.71,845/- and a mattress for Rs.45,800/- on 8 th and 10th June 2016 and demanded that the petitioner pay for it. Crl.Misc.88/2021 3. Further petitioner submitted that, on 24.05.2016 she went to Lucknow with her father in law for her first Vat-Savitri Pooja for that respondent No.1 was also invited and he had promised the petitioner that he would join her but eventually did not turn up for it and later on 06.06.2016 he asked the petitioner to come back to Delhi and demanded to book return tickets by her parents or her brother. Respondent No.1 slowly began alienating the petitioner and stopped taking responsibility for the petitioner both emotionally and financially. Respondent No.1 used to taunt Anamika Jha vs Mayank Mrinal on 7 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/167409963/ 2 and abuse the petitioner frequently and right from around 10 th June 2016 he began threatening the petitioner by telling her that if she didn't accede to his unreasonable demands he would divorce her. Petitioner was interested in teaching and she got interview call from reputed schools at Greater Noida but Respondent No.2 has not allowed her to go for the interview and told her that teaching is a cheap job. Further she submitted that, respondent No.1 was not interested in registering the marriage but finally on 15.07.2016 the petitioner and respondent No.1 got registered their marriage during that time respondent No.2 told the respondent No.1 that he should sign the papers carefully since in case the parties get divorced in the future then the petitioner Crl.Misc.88/2021 would not be entitled to any share in the property. Petitioner was slowly becoming aware that the respondent No.1 and respondent No.2 were already thinking of ways to abandon the petitioner for no rhyme or reason. On 24.07.2016 her parents visited her at matrimonial place for the first time but respondent No.2 was unhappy about their visit and told to her mother that petitioner was cheap and a prostitute because she sat on the sofa beside her husband respondent No.1. 4. Petitioner has alleged that, she found out she was pregnant on 24.07.2016 and very exited to share good news with her family but respondent No.1 fought with her. She has further alleged that, during her pregnancy she was forced to take care of herself with her parent's support since respondent No.1 and their family were detached and abusive. She has alleged that, she was not allowed to rest during her pregnancy because respondent No.2 believed that baby would be born dumb if she slept in the afternoon. She has further alleged that, respondents used to pick up quarrels with her during her pregnancy without being bothered about her and unborn child and also threatened the petitioner that he will give divorce. She has further alleged that, respondent No.2 took all way all her jewelry which she Crl.Misc.88/2021 had kept in the locker. She has further alleged that, on 03.10.2016 when her parents came to her matrimonial home and requested respondent No.2 to send the petitioner to Lucknow for a few days, respondent No.2 denied their request and respondent No.1 also started abusing petitioner and her family. They cursed the petitioner and her family. Since petitioner became terrified for her safety she decided to leave with her parents to Lucknow. Thereafter, respondents did not visit or care for the petitioner during her pregnancy. She has further alleged that, after her son was born on 24.03.2017 respondent No.1 did not even listen to the news and disconnected the call and respondent No.2 fought with petitioner's mother. She has alleged that, the entire medical expenses of the petitioner during delivery and medical expenses of the child came up to Rs.1,15,912/- and the entire vaccination charges amounting up to Rs.50,000/- which are borne by the petitioner's parents. She has further alleged that, even after she went back to the matrimonial home respondents would unnecessarily taunt her, abuse her and pick up fights with her. She has stated that, on 07.08.2017 when her cousin visited her house respondent No.1 picked up a fight with her and threatened her brother and even told her brother that he Crl.Misc.88/2021 had slapped her previous day. Since petitioner's brother realized it would be unsafe for the petitioner to continue live in the matrimonial home he helped her pack her things and he took her to their aunts place in Dwaraka and from there they left to Lucknow to her parents house. She has alleged that, she has left her valuables at respondent's house but respondents refused to give them back to her. She has further alleged that, respondent No.1 never tried to contact the petitioner after the said incident and he has not taken a responsibility of the petitioner and the child. She has stated that, she has sent email to respondent No.1 asking him why he had abandoned her but there was no response from respondent No.1. Even effort for reconciliation from petitioner's Anamika Jha vs Mayank Mrinal on 7 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/167409963/ 3 family have been refused by respondents. She has submitted that, she has studied MBA after taking loan of Rs.15 lakhs from her father and her son is currently studying and respondent No.1 has not taken up any responsibility towards the child. On all these grounds she prays to allow her petition. 5. After the service of notice, respondents appeared before this court through their counsel and filed statement of objection and in the statement of objection respondents have admitted relationship with Crl.Misc.88/2021 the petitioner and admitted that petitioner and respondent No.1 have one child from the wed lock. Further they denied all the other allegations against them. Further they denied that, they never caused domestic violence against the petitioner. On all these grounds they prays to reject the petition filed by the petitioner. 6. The petitioner to substantiate her case has examined herself as PW.1 and got marked Ex.P.1 to 26. The respondent has not tendered himself for further chief examination and cross examination.
texts.arguments: The Hon'ble Supreme Court in Vidyadhar V/s Manik Rao reported in Crl.Misc.88/2021 1999 (3) SCC Anamika Jha vs Mayank Mrinal on 7 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/167409963/ 5 573 has held that "where a party to the suit does not appear into the witness box and state his own case on oath and does not offer himself to be cross examined by the other side, a presumption would arise that the case set up by him is not correct as has been held in a series of decisions passed by various High Courts and the Privy Council....." She has stated that, she has no properties and she has no liabilities. 18. The Hon'ble Supreme Court in Rajanesh V/s Neha reported in (2021) 2 SCC 324 it is held that, when both spouses are earning sufficiently they have to contribute equally towards the expenses of the child. The respondent is duty bound to maintain the child. However, in this case the respondent No.1 is earning more than the petitioner. Since petitioner has the custody of the child and she is residing in a rented house she is incurring expenses towards the education, extra curricular activities, day to day expenses, rent, household expenses, flat maintenance, medical expenses of the child and herself from her income. This is apart from actually taking care of the needs of the child. The income of the petitioner is very much less compared to that of respondent No.1. Respondent No.1 being the father and the husband has to maintain the petitioner Crl.Misc.88/2021 and the child. Even though the petitioner is earning respondent No.1 has a duty to provide for shelter and the expenses of the child. Petitioner has sought for Rs.40,000/- for rent and Rs.1,50,000/- towards security deposit. Apart from that, she has sought for monthly maintenance of Rs.94,000/- and Rs.22,05,912/- for the expenses incurred by her for the cost 5 years, Rs.6,55,000/- towards one time expenses for the petitioner and her child. 19. The petitioner has sought for direction to the respondents to pay compensation and damages of Crl.Misc.88/2021 Rs.1,00,00,000/- for the physical and mental torture suffered at the hands of the respondents and litigation expenses of Rs.2,00,000/-.
